```{r Step 0: Pull in ANES Data, include=TRUE}
anes_panel <- read_dta(here("00_rawdata", "ANES_Data", "anes_timeseries_cdf_stata_20260205.dta"))
```

```{r Step 1: Cleaning Up the Dataset, include=TRUE}
# Check the variables
anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  rename(year = VCF0004, trust_gov_index = VCF0656, trust_gov = VCF0604, econ_views = VCF0870, stock_owns = VCF9224, social_class = VCF0149, person_finances = VCF0880, person_finances_scale = VCF0880a, personal_finances_next = VCF0881, age = VCF0101, age_group = VCF0102, gender = VCF0104, race = VCF0105a, educ = VCF0110, income_group = VCF0114, emp_status = VCF0116, homeowner = VCF0146, marital_stat = VCF0147, partisan_id = VCF0301, partisan_strength = VCF0305, pol_interest = VCF0310, union_mem = VCF0127)

#Turn Dataset into Survey Object
anes_svy <- anes_panel %>%
  filter(year >= 2000) %>%
  as_survey_design(
    ids = 1,
    weights = VCF0009z
  ) 

anes_svy

#Initial Diagnostics
anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    personal_finances_change = case_when(
      as.numeric(person_finances_scale) %in% 1:5 ~ as.numeric(person_finances),
      as.numeric(person_finances) %in% c(8, 9) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    personal_finances_scale_factor = factor(
      personal_finances_change,
      levels = 1:5,
      labels = c(
        "Much better",
        "Somewhat better",
        "Same",
        "Somewhat worse",
        "Much worse"
      )
    )
  )

#Recoding Variables (Brought Over from Part 1)
anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    trust_gov_index = na_if(trust_gov_index, 999)
  )

#Same Thing for Economic Views
anes_panel %>%
  filter(year >= 2000, year <= 2024) %>%
  count(econ_views, sort = TRUE)

#Recode Data to Only show valid entries
anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    trust_gov_index = na_if(trust_gov_index, 999),
    econ_views = case_when(
      econ_views %in% c(1, 3, 5) ~ econ_views,
      econ_views %in% c(8, 9) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    # Trust
    trust_gov_index = if_else(
      trust_gov_index == 999,
      NA_real_,
      as.numeric(trust_gov_index)
    ),

    # Economic views
    econ_views = case_when(
      as.numeric(econ_views) %in% c(1, 3, 5) ~ as.numeric(econ_views),
      as.numeric(econ_views) %in% c(8, 9) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # Stock ownership
    stock_owns = case_when(
      as.numeric(stock_owns) == 1 ~ 1,
      as.numeric(stock_owns) == 2 ~ 0,
      as.numeric(stock_owns) %in% c(-8, -9) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # Homeownership
    homeowner = case_when(
      as.numeric(homeowner) == 1 ~ 1,
      as.numeric(homeowner) == 2 ~ 0,
      as.numeric(homeowner) %in% c(8, 9) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # Income percentile group
    income_group = as.numeric(income_group)
  )

anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    econ_views_factor = factor(
      econ_views,
      levels = c(1, 3, 5),
      labels = c(
        "Get better",
        "Stay about the same",
        "Get worse"
      )
    ),

    income_group_factor = factor(
      income_group,
      levels = 1:5,
      labels = c(
        "0–16th percentile",
        "17–33rd percentile",
        "34–67th percentile",
        "68–95th percentile",
        "96–100th percentile"
      )
    )
  )

anes_panel %>%
  filter(year >= 2000, year <= 2024) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    personal_finances_missing = sum(is.na(personal_finances_change)),
    econ_views_missing = sum(is.na(econ_views_factor))
  )


```

```{r Step 2: Initial Modeling of Raw Relationship Over Time, include=TRUE}
personal_national_models <- lapply(
  sort(unique(anes_panel$year[
    anes_panel$year >= 2000 & anes_panel$year <= 2024
  ])),
  function(y) {

    data_y <- anes_panel %>%
      filter(
        year == y,
        !is.na(personal_finances_change),
        !is.na(econ_views),
        !is.na(VCF0009z)
      )

    if (nrow(data_y) == 0) return(NULL)

    design_y <- survey::svydesign(
      ids = ~1,
      weights = ~VCF0009z,
      data = data_y
    )

    mod <- survey::svyglm(
      econ_views ~ personal_finances_change,
      design = design_y
    )

    broom::tidy(mod) %>%
      filter(term == "personal_finances_change") %>%
      mutate(
        year = y,
        n = nrow(data_y)
      )
  }
) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  select(year, n, everything())

personal_national_models
```

```{r Step 4: Understanding the Income Gradient of the Relationship between Personal Views and National Views, include=TRUE}
personal_income_svy_models <- lapply(
  sort(unique(anes_panel$year[
    anes_panel$year >= 2000 & anes_panel$year <= 2024
  ])),
  function(y) {

    data_y <- anes_panel %>%
      filter(
        year == y,
        !is.na(econ_views),
        !is.na(personal_finances_scale_factor),
        !is.na(income_group_factor),
        !is.na(VCF0009z)
      )

    if (nrow(data_y) == 0) return(NULL)

    design_y <- survey::svydesign(
      ids = ~1,
      weights = ~VCF0009z,
      data = data_y
    )

    mod <- survey::svyglm(
      econ_views ~
        personal_finances_scale_factor *
        income_group_factor,
      design = design_y
    )

    list(
      year = y,
      model = mod,
      n = nrow(data_y)
    )
  }
)

personal_income_svy_models

personal_income_pessimism_contrasts <- lapply(
  personal_income_svy_models,
  function(x) {

    if (is.null(x)) return(NULL)

    out <- marginaleffects::comparisons(
      x$model,
      variables = list(
        personal_finances_scale_factor = c(
          "Much worse",
          "Same"
        )
      ),
      by = "income_group_factor"
    )

    out %>%
      as.data.frame() %>%
      mutate(
        year = x$year,
        n = x$n
      )
  }
) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  select(
    year,
    n,
    income_group_factor,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    p.value,
    conf.low,
    conf.high
  ) %>%
  arrange(year, income_group_factor)

personal_income_pessimism_contrasts

personal_income_gradient_tests <- lapply(
  personal_income_svy_models,
  function(x) {

    if (is.null(x)) return(NULL)

    # Get the Much worse - Same contrast within each income group
    contrasts <- marginaleffects::comparisons(
      x$model,
      variables = list(
        personal_finances_scale_factor = c(
          "Much worse",
          "Same"
        )
      ),
      by = "income_group_factor"
    )

    # Test differences between income-group-specific contrasts
    tests <- marginaleffects::hypotheses(
      contrasts,
      hypothesis = c(
        "b2 - b1 = 0",
        "b3 - b1 = 0",
        "b4 - b1 = 0",
        "b5 - b1 = 0"
      )
    )

    tests %>%
      as.data.frame() %>%
      mutate(
        year = x$year,
        n = x$n
      )
  }
) %>%
  bind_rows()

personal_income_gradient_tests <- lapply(
  personal_income_svy_models,
  function(x) {

    if (is.null(x)) return(NULL)

    contrasts <- marginaleffects::comparisons(

) %>%

personal_income_gradient_tests


mod_2024 <- personal_income_svy_models[
  sapply(
    personal_income_svy_models,
    function(x) !is.null(x) && x$year == 2024
  )
][[1]]$model

interaction_terms <- grep(
  "^personal_finances_scale_factorMuch worse:income_group_factor",
  names(coef(mod_2024)),
  value = TRUE
)

interaction_terms

test_formula <- as.formula(
  paste(
    "~",
    paste(
      sprintf("`%s`", interaction_terms),
      collapse = " + "
    )
  )
)

test_formula

personal_income_joint_tests <- lapply(
  personal_income_svy_models,
  function(x) {

    if (is.null(x)) return(NULL)

    mod <- x$model

    # Identify the four Much worse × income interaction coefficients
    interaction_idx <- grep(
      "^personal_finances_scale_factorMuch worse:income_group_factor",
      names(coef(mod))
    )

    # Extract coefficient vector
    beta <- coef(mod)[interaction_idx]

    # Extract corresponding survey-adjusted covariance matrix
    V <- vcov(mod)[interaction_idx, interaction_idx, drop = FALSE]

    # Wald chi-square statistic
    W <- as.numeric(
      t(beta) %*% solve(V) %*% beta
    )

    # Number of restrictions
    q <- length(beta)

    # Survey design degrees of freedom
    df_den <- survey::degf(mod$survey.design)

    # Convert Wald statistic to F
    F_stat <- W / q

    # F-test p-value
    p_value <- pf(
      F_stat,
      df1 = q,
      df2 = df_den,
      lower.tail = FALSE
    )

    data.frame(
      year = x$year,
      n = x$n,
      F = F_stat,
      df_num = q,
      df_den = df_den,
      p.value = p_value
    )
  }
) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  arrange(year)

personal_income_joint_tests
#No evidence of income moderation across waves, though there is a consistent relationship between personal finances and views of the national economy
```

```{r Step 5: Moderation by Stock Ownership, include=TRUE}
    F_stat <- W / q

    df_den <- mod$df.residual

    p_value <- pf(
      F_stat,
      df1 = q,
      df2 = df_den,
      lower.tail = FALSE

    data.frame(
      year = x$year,
      n = x$n,
      F = F_stat,
      df_num = q,
      df_den = df_den,
      p.value = p_value

#In 2024, the correspondence between changes in respondents' personal financial circumstances and their perceptions of the national economy was substantially stronger among stock owners than among non-stock owners.

personal_stock_direction_joint_plot <- ggplot(
  personal_stock_direction_joint_tests,
  aes(x = year, y = F)
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = qf(0.95, df1 = 2, df2 = 10000),
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(2000, 2002, 2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020, 2024)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "F-statistic",
    title = "Stock Ownership Moderation of the Personal–National Economic Relationship",
    subtitle = "Joint test of the personal-finance × stock-ownership interaction"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)
  )

personal_stock_direction_joint_plot
```
